findings.explanation: The SPL computes offline_min from the age of the latest event, not the time the camera has been offline, and the 1-hour default poll interval in the same text makes a 15-minute threshold unachievable. No 15-minute test appears in the SPL.
findings.quote: Alert when any MV reports `status="offline"` for more than 15 minutes
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to alert on the latest polled status being offline and note the poll interval is the detection floor, or lower the polling interval.

findings.explanation: The use case's own add-on is Splunkbase 5580 (Cisco Meraki Add-on for Splunk, Splunk_TA_cisco_meraki); 5631 is not in the cached catalog and is presented as a second add-on of a different name.
findings.suggested_fix: Check what Splunkbase 5631 is; remove it or correct the title.

findings.explanation: The Meraki devices/availabilities API returns serial, name, mac, network id, productType and status; `model` and `network.name` may only exist on the devices inventory, not on meraki:devicesavailabilities.
findings.suggested_fix: Check sample meraki:devicesavailabilities events for model and network.name; if absent, enrich with the devices sourcetype.

findings.explanation: The detection only shows polled status; it does not prove recording gaps or any compliance outcome.
findings.quote: sustained offline cameras break recorded coverage and create compliance gaps.
findings.suggested_fix: Say offline cameras may leave recording gaps; confirm with the video retention records.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: offline_min = now() - latest(_time) measures how stale the newest event is, not how long the camera has been offline; the label offline_min is misleading.

summary: A reasonable Meraki camera-availability search, but the 15-minute offline rule is not computed by the SPL and the TA reference conflicts with the grounded Splunkbase ID. Field availability on the availabilities sourcetype needs checking.
